name: Dasatinib (CML, chronic phase, first-line)

biomarkers.note: CML is defined by the BCR::ABL1 fusion (Philadelphia chromosome); confirm Ph-positive or BCR::ABL1-positive by qPCR at diagnosis. A T315I kinase-domain mutation confers resistance to dasatinib (and to imatinib, nilotinib and bosutinib); ponatinib or asciminib is the treatment option for T315I. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Chronic Myeloid Leukemia v2.2027.

lineOfTherapy: first-line for newly diagnosed chronic-phase CML (a second-generation TKI)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: BCR::ABL1-positive (Ph-positive) chronic-phase CML confirmed by qPCR
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2027, CML workup (Ph-positive or BCR::ABL1 positive by qPCR)

drugs.name: Dasatinib

provenance.locator: MS-27 (recommended starting dose of dasatinib is 100 mg once daily for CP-CML)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Chronic Myeloid Leukemia v2.2027, MS-27. Dasatinib 100 mg PO once daily, continuous. Days 1 to 28 represents continuous daily dosing. A reduced dose (for example 50 mg once daily) is described for clinically significant intolerance such as pleural effusion (MS-27). Continue until loss of response, progression or intolerance.

supportiveCare: Continuous daily oral therapy; adherence is critical to maintaining molecular response.
Dasatinib is associated with pleural effusion (higher risk with prior cardiac history, hypertension, or twice-daily dosing); assess respiratory symptoms and consider dose reduction.
Monitor BCR::ABL1 (IS) by qPCR at milestones; if resistance, test for kinase-domain mutations (T315I directs ponatinib or asciminib).

monitoring: CBC with differential at baseline and periodically
BCR::ABL1 (IS) by qPCR at approximately 3, 6 and 12 months and periodically thereafter (CML-G)
assessment for pleural effusion (dyspnea, chest exam) and fluid retention

doseModificationRules.condition: pleural effusion or grade 3 to 4 toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt for significant toxicity; consider resuming at a reduced dose (for example 50 mg once daily) for clinically significant intolerance such as pleural effusion (MS-27). Physician decides.

guideline.locator: MS-27 (recommended starting dose of dasatinib is 100 mg once daily for CP-CML; reduced 50 mg option for intolerance/pleural effusion); T315I/ponatinib option (manuscript and CML footnote)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for first-line dasatinib (a second-generation TKI) in chronic-phase, BCR::ABL1-positive CML.
